q-331457.source_quote:
Therefore, the Laplace transform of $f(t)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =L{{e}^{3t}}-L{{e}^{-t}} \\  & =\frac{1}{s-3}-\frac{1}{s+1} \\  & =\frac{(s+1)-(s-3)}{(s-3)(s+1)} \\  & =\frac{s+1-s+3}{(s-3)(s+1)} \\  & =\frac{4}{(s-3)(s+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-49431.binding: The sole radio field selection asks for the indefinite integral in z. The aligned integration calculation ends with -2/9 sqrt(1-9z)+C before the differentiation check; original choice c, index 2, preserves the full antiderivative and constant.
q-49431.source_quote:
We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $u$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1-9z)^{-1/2}\,\text{d}z & =\int {u}^{-1/2}\cdot (-\frac{1}{9}\text{d}u) \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}\int {u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}\frac{1}{(1/2)}{u}^{1/2}+C \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}{u}^{1/2}+C \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}(1-9z)^{1/2}+C \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{1-9z}+C\end{aligned}
$$
